repo_notes.content: GamePreset Peek is a Windows desktop application in Python 3.13 with a Qt user interface (PySide6-Essentials). It shows the optimal game settings NVIDIA recommends for the user's processor, graphics card, memory and screen resolution, without NVIDIA App. Runtime dependencies are requests, fake-useragent, loguru and PySide6-Essentials; the theme is the project's own package src/app/ui/flat_theme (reworked from PyQtDarkTheme). The source of truth is the code under src/app and tests: cite code files first and use .claude/notes.md and README.md only for the reasons behind a design.

Module names, to be used exactly as they are: src/app/core holds app_db.py (read-only SQLite connections), database.py (AppDatabase: loading and updating the bundled database), game_catalog.py (GameCatalog), game_finder.py (GameFinder and WindowsRegistry: installed games), covers.py (CoverCache: box art), hardware.py (hardware detection, CpuList, GpuList, GpuRanks), screen_shape.py, models.py, ops_api.py (OpsApi), service.py (PresetService) and user_settings.py. src/app/infra holds app_dirs.py, elevation.py, http_client.py and logger.py. src/app/i18n holds translator.py and ui_text.py. Everything else of the UI is in src/app/ui. There are no modules named game_names.py or cover_cache.py.

Network use: the recommended presets, the presets files and the translations are requested from NVIDIA's servers when the user picks a game, so the main feature needs an internet connection. Only the game list, the CPU and GPU lists and the GPU ranks come from the bundled database and are available offline. Describe the app as needing no NVIDIA account and no NVIDIA App, not as offline-first.

Box art: the URL of each game's cover is stored in the bundled database and downloaded with ;f=jpg;w=COVER_WIDTH, then cached on disk under the sha256 of the URL. NVIDIA's GraphQL service (NV_GAME_ART_URL) is asked only as a fallback, when downloading the stored URL fails with an HTTP error; the picture found then is cached under the failed URL's file name.

The bundled database src/app/data/app.db is written by a separate private project that owns its schema and updates it weekly; this repository only reads it. After each weekly run that project commits the manifest data/app.db.json (sha256 of the database and the time of the check). The app reads the manifest from DB_MANIFEST_URL when its last check is older than the last Monday 03:00 UTC (DB_CHECK_WEEKDAY, DB_CHECK_TIME) and downloads DB_UPDATE_URL only when the sha256 differs. The download goes to app.download beside the file, must match the manifest's sha256, is validated by loading every list from it and then replaces app.db with os.replace.

Running from source on Windows, from the repository root: create and activate the .venv virtualenv, run pip install -r src/requirements.txt -r src/requirements-dev.txt (the dev file only constrains, so both are installed), compile the translations with infrastructure\localization\3.compile_translations.cmd (the app needs the compiled .mo files), then set PYTHONPATH to src and run python -m app (PowerShell: $env:PYTHONPATH="src"; python -m app). Checks: black src tests, mypy src tests, pylint -j 2 src tests (score 10), pytest, and coverage run --source=src/app -m pytest with 100 % line coverage required.

Mermaid diagrams must render: put every node label and every message text in double quotes, keep labels on one line, and use no parentheses, slashes, dots or colons in node identifiers (use short ids like svc, ops, db and put the file path in the quoted label).
